subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Aurora Retail discovery
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@auroraretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@auroraretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Aurora Retail discovery

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps while it’s fresh: 

Summary of discovery:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for inference serving across web checkout (low-latency scoring) and personalized recommendation batch workloads.
- Primary constraints: sub-100ms p95 latency for checkout, SOC 2 + data residency for EU transactions, procurement prefers annual contract with committed capacity.
- Current infra: AWS us-west + eu-west accounts, internal platform team owns deployment, procurement handles vendor onboarding.

Key decision criteria you mentioned:
1) Latency and reliability under peak checkout traffic
2) Clear security/compliance evidence (SOC 2, data handling controls)
3) Pricing predictability for peak season
4) Integration effort with existing infra and CD pipeline

Proposed next steps:
- Could you share a short stakeholder map (org chart or list) with the following roles identified: economic buyer, procurement/legal contact, security/compliance reviewer, and platform/infra owner? (If multiple people per role, that’s fine.)
- We’ll follow up with a short tailored doc that maps Redwood capabilities -> your decision criteria and recommended next steps for procurement/security.
- Schedule a 30m tech deep-dive with your infra team (Rishi and Marissa to join) — availability next week?

If helpful, I can draft a one-pager that calls out exactly what evidence procurement/security will want (SOC 2 report, data flow diagrams, retention policies).

Thanks — looking forward to the mapping.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@auroraretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@auroraretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Aurora Retail discovery

Thanks Neha — good recap. Attaching a quick org sketch (high-level) — we’ll follow up with formal org chart tomorrow. For now: 

- Economic buyer: Priya Shah (VP Retail Ops) — priya.shah@auroraretail.com
- Procurement: procurement@auroraretail.com (managed by Elena Gomez)
- Security/compliance reviewer: Marcus Lee (Senior InfoSec Engineer) — marcus.lee@auroraretail.com
- Platform owner: Jamie Torres (Head of Platform) — me

Two notes on process: 
1) Procurement will require SOC 2 Type II and a vendor questionnaire (we’ll send a starter questionnaire once legal signs off).
2) For pricing, procurement asks for committed throughput options + overage rates — they tend to prefer a predictable monthly commit.

We’re happy to set up the tech deep-dive — Tue/Wed next week between 10–2 PT should work.

Link to internal procurement intake: https://aurora.atlassian.net/browse/PR-4422 (for your team to reference)

On the org chart: attaching "Aurora_OrgChart_v1.pdf" — it’s very light but shows the reporting lines.

—Jamie

Attachment: Aurora_OrgChart_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700

Looping in Rishi —

Couple quick asks to prepare before the tech deep-dive: 
- Rishi: can you prepare a 10-slide tech brief focusing on p95 tail latency improvements, caching strategies (prefix KV caching) for checkout scoring, and a suggested quantization profile for their recommended model size?
- Also draft a short slide that maps required security artifacts (SOC 2, data flow diagram, contract clauses) to where they live in our console/docs so procurement can easily find them.

I’ll draft the meeting invite for Tue 10:30 PT and include the procurement contact so they can join if needed.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Thanks Jamie — appreciate the org chart. Next steps from our side: 

1) I’ll send a short one-pager today that maps Redwood artifacts to procurement/security asks (SOC 2 link, data flow diagram, retention policy, support SLAs).
2) Marissa and Rishi will join the tech deep-dive tomorrow, Tue 10:30 PT (calendar invite to follow).
3) We’ll include procurement (Elena) on the invite — if procurement prefers, we can do a separate 20–30m session to walk through the questionnaire.

Questions for you ahead of the session: 
- Do you have a preferred NDA or do you want us to use our standard mutual NDA? 
- Any constraints around data residency for EU checkout traffic beyond eu-west hosting?

If you reply with those two items we’ll finalize materials.

Best,
Neha
